# 出生無邊門陀羅尼經

**Dynasty:** 唐

## Contributors
- 智嚴 (A001302)

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A one-fascicle early-Tang translation of the *Anantamukha-sādhaka-dhāraṇī* by **Zhìyán** ([智嚴](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E5%9A%B4), fl. early 8th c.), the Khotanese (于闐) prince-translator. The text shares its **Chinese title in full** with Amoghavajra's later T1009 ([KR6j0202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0202)) — both bear the title *Chūshēng wúbiānmén tuóluóní jīng*, distinguished only by translator and date. CANWWW alt-title: *Wúbiānmén tuóluóní jīng* 無邊門陀羅尼經.

**Abstract**

Zhìyán was a prince of the **Yútián** 于闐 (Khotan) royal house who took monastic ordination and travelled to Chángān, where he served the Tang court as imperial translator. His most celebrated work is the present *Anantamukha* translation, made in 721 ([玄宗](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E7%8E%84%E5%AE%97) Xuánzōng Kāiyuán 9) and recorded in *Kāiyuán shìjiào lù* 開元釋教錄 — a date that puts him precisely in the generation between Bodhiruci II [菩提流志](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%8F%A9%E6%8F%90%E6%B5%81%E5%BF%97) (active 706–727) and Vajrabodhi [金剛智](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%87%91%E5%89%9B%E6%99%BA) (671–741, arrived 720). His translation thus represents the final pre-Esoteric phase of the *Anantamukha* tradition in Chinese, immediately preceding Amoghavajra's eighth-century re-translation [KR6j0202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0202) within the systematic Tángmì programme. Listed at Nanjio 360. For the full Anantamukha translation cycle, see [KR6j0202](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6j/KR6j0202).
